fact_text: A US election outcome seen as lowering the odds of continued war with Iran lifted world equities and pushed oil down, because reopening of the Strait of Hormuz was expected to ease the oil price premium.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst attributed elevated oil prices to the Iran war and the Hormuz disruption, so peace hopes translate directly into falling crude prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A political camp seen as anti-AI because of job-loss fears triggered a sharp fall in US AI and technology stocks, which had been driving the US market boom.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argued that Pakistani macro numbers were good and the PSX lagged mainly because of geopolitics, so any positive war-related news produced a quick rally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expected PSX performance to depend largely on whether US-Iran peace talks, now including Iran's nuclear capabilities, materialise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A Qatar-to-Pakistan LNG tanker was attacked during the war even though Pakistan had sought Iranian permission for passage, showing supply-route risk for imported energy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank of Pakistan's inflation target range is 5 to 7 percent, and double-digit inflation was the stated reason for it raising its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To block an expected rise of about Rs15 per litre in petrol, the government cut the petroleum development levy by about Rs15 from Rs80 and shifted the burden onto refineries.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Petrol import premiums rose from about $5 per barrel before the war to about $25-30 per barrel on PSO cargoes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the revised formula, import price follows the premium PSO actually pays, but ex-refinery price is pinned to pre-war levels, leaving refineries absorbing the gap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Refineries estimated the pricing change as a burden of about Rs40-50 per litre, which could push them to a negative gross margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Listed refinery stocks hit lower circuits when the government shifted fuel price burden onto refineries, showing high sensitivity to pricing-formula policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Refineries signed a $5-6 billion upgrade plan with the government that needs heavy capex, so squeezed margins from the pricing formula threaten funding ability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With international oil prices falling, the analyst noted the government might withdraw the one-month pricing relief, which would ease the refinery burden.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Holding down petrol prices benefits consumers but is a cost transferred to refineries, so fuel relief and refinery earnings move in opposite directions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The federal cabinet approved new designs for Rs50, 100, 500, 1000 and 5000 notes while old notes stay in circulation, and the Rs10 note will be discontinued in favour of a coin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The digital microfinance bank's book-building IPO was 1.6 times subscribed at a strike price of Rs15.50 against a Rs15 floor, raising about Rs2.05 billion from 99 million shares.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst saw the digital microfinance bank IPO as significant mainly because it was the first successful fintech IPO in Pakistan, with 33 million shares reserved for retail.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A digital lending fintech filed a draft prospectus to list about 50.16 million shares at Rs1 face value, floor Rs8.75, price band up to about Rs13, with 75% book-building and 25% retail.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New brokerage accounts rose to a record in one month, with Gen Z and millennials about 89% of accounts and Sahulat accounts about 77%, indicating broadening retail participation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Hum Network's consolidated net profit fell about 87% to Rs42.38 million versus Rs315.9 million a year earlier despite revenue up 17% to Rs2.05 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: City Pharma's revenue rose about 4.3% to Rs3.5 billion and profit rose about 22% to roughly Rs250 million, with EPS Rs1.09 versus Rs0.89.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan Aluminium Beverage Cans revenue fell about 52% to Rs3.5 billion from Rs7.49 billion, and profit fell about 26% to Rs1.3 billion, with EPS Rs3.61 versus Rs4.89.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'New Currency Notes, Petrol Prices Fall, 2 IPOs | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)
